### Building a New PC – A Step‑by‑Step Guide Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough. Feel free to skip sections you already know, but keep the order to avoid missing anything. | # | Step | What to Do | Tips | |---|------|------------|------| | 1 | **Plan & Budget** | • Decide what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, general use).
• Set a budget (CPU, GPU, RAM, storage, case, PSU, peripherals). | Use online PC builders (e.g., PCPartPicker) to check compatibility and price. | | 2 | **Gather Tools & Workspace** | • Phillips screwdriver (magnetic tip).
• Anti‑static wrist strap or mat.
• Clean, flat surface. | Keep the area dust‑free; a clean workspace reduces static damage. | | 3 | **Choose Components** | • **CPU** (Intel/AMD).
• **Motherboard** (socket, chipset, form factor).
• **RAM** (DDR4/DDR5, speed, capacity).
• **GPU** (if not integrated).
• **Storage** (NVMe SSD, SATA SSD/HDD).
• **Case** (ATX, mATX, mini‑ITX).
• **Power Supply** (80+ Gold, wattage).
• **Cooling** (stock cooler, aftermarket air, or AIO liquid). | Verify all parts are compatible (socket, BIOS, power connectors). | | 4 | **Prepare the Case** | • Remove side panels.
• Install standoffs for the motherboard.
• Mount the PSU (usually at the bottom or top rear). | Some cases have pre‑installed standoffs; check the manual. | | 5 | **Install the CPU** | • Open the CPU socket latch.
• Align the CPU (triangle marker) with the socket.
• Gently place it, then lock the latch. | Don’t force; the CPU will fit snugly. | | 6 | **Apply Thermal Paste & Mount Cooler** | • If using an aftermarket cooler, apply a pea‑size amount of thermal paste.
• Attach the cooler per its instructions. | Avoid over‑applying paste; too much can spill into the CPU. | | 7 | **Insert RAM** | • Open the RAM slots’ clips.
• Align the notch on the RAM with the slot.
• Push firmly until the clips click. | Install in the recommended slots (often 1 & 3 for dual‑channel). | | 8 | **Mount the Motherboard** | • Align the motherboard with the standoffs and I/O shield.
• Secure with screws. | Double‑check that all screw holes line up. | | 9 | **Install Storage** | • NVMe SSD: slide into the M.2 slot, secure with a screw.
• SATA SSD/HDD: mount in a drive bay, connect SATA data & power cables. | Label cables if you have many drives. | | 10 | **Install the GPU** | • Remove the appropriate expansion slot covers on the case.
• Insert the GPU into the top PCI‑e x16 slot.
• Secure with screws.
• Connect 6‑pin/8‑pin PCI‑e power cables. | Ensure the GPU is fully seated; it should click into place. | | 11 | **Connect Power Cables** | • 24‑pin ATX to motherboard.
• 8‑pin EPS to CPU.
• SATA power to drives.
• PCI‑e power to GPU. | Keep cables organized; use cable ties if needed. | | 12 | **Cable Management** | • Route cables behind the motherboard tray.
• Use Velcro ties or zip ties.
• Leave enough slack for airflow. | Good cable management improves airflow and makes future upgrades easier. | | 13 | **Final Checks** | • Verify all connections.
• Ensure no loose screws or cables.
• Check that the case fans are connected. | Double‑check the BIOS jumpers if you’re using a new motherboard. | | 14 | **Power On & BIOS Setup** | • Connect monitor, keyboard, mouse.
• Turn on the PSU switch.
• Press the power button.
• Enter BIOS (usually **Del** or **F2**). | Set boot priority to your OS drive. Update BIOS if needed. | | 15 | **Install Operating System** | • Create a bootable USB (Windows 10/11, Ubuntu, etc.).
• Boot from USB, follow installation prompts. | Install drivers after OS installation (GPU, chipset, Wi‑Fi). | | 16 | **Install Drivers & Software** | • Download latest GPU drivers (NVIDIA/AMD).
• Install motherboard chipset drivers.
• Install any other peripheral drivers. | Keep your system updated for stability and performance. | | 17 | **Test & Benchmark** | • Run stress tests (Prime95, 3DMark, Cinebench).
• Monitor temperatures (HWMonitor, MSI Afterburner). | Ensure temperatures stay within safe limits (CPU < 80 °C, GPU < 85 °C). | | 18 | **Enjoy & Maintain** | • Keep the case dust‑free.
• Update firmware and drivers regularly.
• Monitor performance. | Regular cleaning (fans, vents) keeps airflow optimal. | --- #### Quick Checklist - [ ] CPU + cooler installed - [ ] RAM seated - [ ] Motherboard mounted - [ ] PSU installed - [ ] GPU seated & powered - [ ] Storage installed - [ ] All power cables connected - [ ] Cables managed - [ ] BIOS set to boot from OS drive - [ ] OS installed - [ ] Drivers installed - [ ] Benchmarked & temperatures checked --- #### Common Pitfalls & Fixes | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | **PC doesn’t power on** | Check PSU switch, ensure all power cables are connected, verify that the motherboard has a POST LED or speaker. | | **No display** | Confirm GPU is seated, check monitor input, try a different cable, test with a known‑working GPU. | | **Overheating** | Reapply thermal paste, improve cable routing, add case fans, clean dust. | | **Component incompatibility** | Use PCPartPicker’s “Check Compatibility” feature before buying. | --- #### Resources - **PCPartPicker** – Build & compare parts, check compatibility. - **YouTube Channels** – Linus Tech Tips, JayzTwoCents, Paul's Hardware. - **Reddit** – r/buildapc for community help. - **Manufacturer Manuals** – Always read the motherboard, PSU, and case manuals. Happy building! If you hit a snag, let me know which step and I’ll help troubleshoot.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "How to build a new PC?" They want instructions. We can provide a step-by-step guide. No function call needed.
